argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a caveated deployment-readiness determination, not as a clean no-limitations finding. Aggregate readiness clears launch by 2.2 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports overall readiness. The same record also shows a remaining weakness in student aid advising, concentrated in dependency-status appeal guidance, and a draft mitigation runbook with required fields still incomplete. The defensible packet therefore narrows the claim: certify for launch readiness while explicitly disclosing the known limitation, and do not treat the current record as proving absence of material limitations.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit concern. The narrower caveated-certification framing preserves the locked certification action while reducing governance risk from overclaiming beyond the admissible record.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support clean certification without caveats on the present record. It requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current runbook is still draft and missing required elements, so it cannot remove the disclosure requirement. The policy is satisfied more credibly if the audit packet treats certification as caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the student aid limitation rather than as an unqualified no-issues determination.
concessions: The present record does not support any clean statement that there are no known material limitations.
The draft mitigation runbook is not yet sufficient as approved mitigation under the stated policy.
If the model-card continues to say there are no known material limitations without correcting for the student aid issue, the case for compliance weakens materially.
